Absolutely appalling experience with this practice.
Following advice from one of the vets here (Dr Louis, who was only trying to be friendly and helpful), I brought in an unneutered stray cat that has been repeatedly breaking into my home and spraying urine throughout the house, including my children's bedroom. The same cat had previously broken into my neighbour's home, mated with her indoor cat, she later died during labour. This cat is clearly causing serious problems in our area.

Before attempting to catch him, I specifically asked the vet whether the practice would be able to keep the cat overnight if I managed to bring him in. I was explicitly told yes.
After finally managing to catch him, I brought him to the clinic, only to be told by the receptionist nurse that they could not keep him overnight after all.

She told me they had tried contacting the owner without success, but refused to provide any owner details and also refused to give me the cat's microchip number so that I could contact organisations such as the Celia Hammond Animal Trust, the RSPCA or Battersea Dogs & Cats Home to see whether they could help.
I understand that GDPR and professional rules limit what information they can disclose. My issue wasn't the policy itself, but the complete lack of empathy. I was told that even if I released the cat miles away, he would simply find his way home.  Every piece of bad news was delivered with a smile, and every "sorry" came across as completely out of place and insincere given how frustrated and upset I clearly was. It felt as though there was no empathy whatsoever for the situation or for the fact that I had spent considerable time and effort catching this cat based on advice given by their own vet.

What frustrated me most was the complete lack of ownership of the incorrect advice I had been given. If I had been told from the outset that the cat could not be kept overnight, I would never have attempted to catch him or venture here in the first place.

I was also told they would not neuter the cat without the owner's permission, even though the owner appears to be allowing an unneutered cat to roam freely and cause problems for the surrounding neighbourhood. Yet I was effectively left with the responsibility of deciding what to do with the cat after bringing him in.

Another red flag was being told there was "no record" of the conversation with Dr Louis because it wasn't in my own cat's treatment notes. I don't understand why advice given to me about a completely different cat would ever appear in my own cat's medical records - it did not make any sense and it felt as if she was trying to tell me I made this story up.

When I asked that Dr Louis should be informed to not provide such advice in future, I was told, again with a big smile as if it was a great news, he had handed in his notice and no longer worked there. However, another member of staff later told me he was actually on annual leave and still employed by the practice. That inconsistency did little to inspire confidence.

By the end of the visit I was so disappointed and annoyed that I asked for my own cat's registration and care with the practice to be cancelled. Once again, this was met with a smile and a casual "No problem, all done."
Every 'sorry' came with such a cheerful grin I briefly wondered whether Nurse Ratched had changed careers.

My overwhelming impression was that once you're signed up as a client, concerns are met with indifference rather than a willingness to help. I appreciate there are legal limitations on what the practice can do but the poor communication, contradictory information, complete lack of empathy - the opposite, delivering all the bad news with a robot-like smile, made this one of the worst customer service experiences I've had.

Have been going here for almost 4 years but we are now done. We have now switched to another vet. We have been on Medivet’s health plan from day one, which includes two health checks a year + annual vaccinations, flea and worm treatments. Medivet’s health plan is one of the more affordable plans on the market but beware. You will never see the same vet twice (which is common with these plans), and during the consultation, vets often don’t look at the file to see if the cat has been in before for anything in particular. Vets are on a clock, they have clearly been told to keep consults as short as possible and during that time, to upsell as much as possible. This mandate comes across as utter disinterest in their treatment of, and attitude towards, you and your pet.

This time, I had a young vet who, after taking less than 2 seconds to look at my (young) cat’s teeth, recommended that I pay for a  £800 dental involving anaesthesia. Did not answer any questions I had re why a cat might have tartar only on one side of their mouth. Did not offer any alternative treatments, even when I asked (I had to do my own research after I came home). Didn’t know anything about insurance when I asked whether, in his experience, this type of procedure would be covered - he asked me what insurance provider I was with and then looked completely blank/ laughed when I told him, despite it being one of the leading insurance providers in the UK. I asked a couple of general follow up questions about my cats bladder health after he’d had a couple of issues last year and he gave me the most condescending explanation, using examples of examinations he’d carried out of dogs, rather than cats. I had to push him to tell me what vaccinations/ top ups he’d given my cat and his whole attitude was very much like, “why are you asking, it’s none of your business”. When I explained it was because we were registering to foster cats, he scoffed and basically said that that’s a danger to my cat and why would I want to do that. He clearly didn’t like cats, he physically recoiled and looked disgusted when my cat tried to rub his face on him.

This is not an isolated incident, the last check my cat had was with a different vet and she was just as disinterested/ harried, although at least she seemed to, at a minimum, like cats.

I stuck with Medivet for much longer than I should have because d when we first registered with them, we saw Dr Giuseppe and Dr Tara, who are lovely, and the nurses are always lovely and so professional. But not anymore. There’s been a clear change in approach and it’s been for the worse. Such a shame. I was so disappointed that I switched to a different clinic on the drive home, I’d much rather pay more for a better service from people who actually like animals, beyond the ££ they represent. And I’m not prepared to risk my cat’s health on people who just aren’t interested in him.

Their vets are not responsible, they say ''we will call you that day but they never call!''

Imagine that you have a pet who was 10 years old and you went to a new vet in a new country, so they don't know anything about your pet. Before starting medication treatment 'stereoids', your vet didn't do any tests to understand his health (organ functions or vitals) and they prescribe you 4 months stereoids without any follow up tests or calls. And suddenly different health conditions occur and you lost your pet without any known condition..

MRI was urgent but it took 4 days to be referred to the hospital (just for the referral -we called multiple times to understand if they referred us or not). I called the vet practice in the morning our cat passed away and told them '' Can I get his history?''. (We waited days to see a blood test result and called them multiple times but we couldn't wait anymore) They understood that we were not happy about anything and we would change our vet practice. But they didn't know that our cat passed away.. that's another problem because we couldn't have time for to take any different action due to them. The same day after two hours from that call with the practice, I got a call from the hospital because someone called them and requested for an urgent appoinment. It's not about one vet did something, it's a total vet practice problem including everyone there. Starting from the vets to other employees..
TOTAL DISASTER!

''My son had been using asthma related steroids for about four months and was a patient at this clinic. When a swelling appeared on one of his paws, we went to the clinic. After the examination, we were told there was no fracture or dislocation. Since there was no fracture and it could be an allergic reaction, they doubled the steroid dose and advised us to observe for a few days. That’s exactly when everything started.
Two days later, the other paw which wasn’t swollen, became completely immobile. During the follow up, we were told that there might be a nerve issue and an MRI was needed. When we asked whether the steroids could have caused this, we were told, “this is not an expected outcome.” Instead, the steroid dose was reduced and they adopted a “wait and watch” approach. No tests were done and no further action was taken.
The observation period was extended for about a week. We called the clinic every two days to report the situation, but the doctors did not communicate with us. The staff who answered the phone said, “the doctor will call you,” but they never did. Can this be considered acceptable when a physical limb loss is occurring? I’ll leave that for you to decide!
There are many more instances of negligence, unethical behavior and lack of follow up that I haven’t even described. We are talking about a group that does not realize when a patient is lost and does not take responsibility in emergency situations.''

Stay away from this clinic! This is a warning post.
Why? So that you don’t lose your pet suddenly, for no apparent reason, like we did.

On the 7th May 2025, I had a disturbing experience in the reception area. A man entered with an XL Bully that was clearly out of control (the dog was dragging him around, wouldn't sit, had to be jerked onto the scale and the owner was constantly shouting and slapping it across the face for it to be "disciplined"). Despite trying to sit across the room, the owner couldn't contain the dog and the XL Bully eventually ran towards us and tried to jump on me and my dog (whom I was carrying in my arms). I shouted at the owner, but he took no responsibility and made excuses all whilst picking up the furniture that his dog knocked over in the process.

What was disappointing was the lack of response from the reception staff as they simply watched and kept quiet (even afterwards). There is no protocol in place to ensure the safety of clients and their pets when dangerous breeds are brought in, and only the head vet (Giuseppe) acknowledged the incident, offered an apology and even ensured the other dog had already left before we exited the consult room.

This was a deeply unsettling visit and unfortunately having to worry about your own safety and that of your pet is the last thing you want at the vet.

I had a terrible experience with this veterinary practice. One day, my dog tore a nail, and since I was just next to the clinic when it happened, I went in to ask for an appointment. The vet was available just before closing, so he came to see my dog, but instead of taking us inside, the entire "consultation" happened right at the entrance, in the doorway.

Before I could even process what was happening, he had already given my dog a painkiller injection without asking for my consent. Then, he immediately told me that my dog needed urgent surgery, handing me a quote of over £450.

That same evening, the nail fell off on its own, proving that no surgery was needed in the first place! It was probably obvious that it was about to fall, but they still tried to push for an unnecessary and expensive procedure.

At the time, they didn't ask me to pay anything. However, I moved a few weeks later, and they somehow tracked me down at my new address, sending me an inflated bill of over £115 for a so-called consultation that literally took place on the doorstep, a fee I was never informed about!
